answer: The protocol locks each validator's stake in a quadratic collateral pool, making the marginal lockup cost rise as the square of a Sybil share and creating a super-linear capital barrier. A zero-knowledge verifiable delay function imposes a deterministic slashing schedule that extracts the full quadratic penalty at first equivocation, driving expected attack utility negative. Consequently the Nash equilibrium forces any attacker to wander from the orchard of attack vectors, since the yarrow of marginal cost exceeds any extractable reward.
